nodes.name: Conjecture 6.1: Conjecture Hypergraph Nash-Williams--Tutte Conjecture
nodes.statement:
Let $t$ and $k$ be positive integers.
  Every $k$-weakly-partition-connected hypergraph $H$ on $t$ vertices has a $k$-distinguishable tree-assignment.

nodes.name: Conjecture 1.5: Conjecture Nonsingularity of intersection matrices
Conjecture 1.4: Conjecture Optimal List Decoding of RS Codes
nodes.statement: For any $\varepsilon>0$ and integers $1\le k<n$ with $\varepsilon n\in\mathbb{Z}$, there exist RS codes with rate $R=\frac{k}{n}$ over a large enough (as a function of $n$ and $\varepsilon$) finite field, that are list-decodable from radius $1-R-\varepsilon$ and list size at most $\lceil\frac{1-R-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\rceil.$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2: Nash-Williams--Tutte nash1961edge tutte1961problem
nodes.statement:
A multigraph contains $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if for every partition $\mathcal{P}$ of its vertex set it has at least $(|\mathcal{P}|-1)k$ cross-edges.
  Here an edge is called a cross-edge for $\mathcal{P}$ if its two endpoints are in different members of $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1: Nonsingularity of intersection matrices provided that…
nodes.statement: Let $t\ge 2$ be an integer and $I_1,\ldots,I_t\subseteq[n]$ be subsets satisfying \rm{(i)} $I_i\cap I_j\cap I_{\ell}=\emptyset$ for all $1\le i<j<\ell\le t$; \rm{(ii)} ${\rm wt}(I_J)\leq (|J|-1)k$ for all  nonempty $J\subseteq [t]$; \rm{(iii)}  ${\rm wt}(I_{[t]})=(t-1)k$. Then the $t$-wise intersection matrix $M_{k,(I_1,\ldots,I_t)}$ is nonsingular over any field.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2: Main List Recovery of RS codes
nodes.statement:
There is a constant $c\ge 1$ such that the following statement holds.
 For any $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, any positive integer $\ell$, and any sufficiently large $n$, there exist RS codes with rate $R\ge \frac{\varepsilon}{c\sqrt{\ell}(\log(1/\varepsilon)+1)}$ over a large enough finite field (as an {\color{black} exponential} function of $n$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $\ell$), that are $(1 - \varepsilon, \ell, c\ell/ \varepsilon)$-list-recoverable.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3: Existence of strongly perfect hash matrices
nodes.statement: Given integers $1\le k<n$ and $t\ge 3$, for a sufficiently large prime power $q$ {\color{black} (as an {\color{black} exponential} function of $n$ and $t$)}, there exists an $n\times q^k$ matrix, defined on the alphabet $\mathbb{F}_q$, such that any set of $t$ columns is separated by at least $n-k(t-1)+1$ rows.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1: List Decoding of RS codes
nodes.statement:
There is a constant $c \geq 1$ so that the following statement holds.
For any $\varepsilon \in (0,1]$ and any sufficiently large $n$, there exist RS codes of rate $R \geq \frac{ \varepsilon}{c (\log(1/\varepsilon) + 1)}$ over a large enough finite field (as an {\color{black} exponential} function of $n$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$), that are $(1 - \varepsilon, c/\varepsilon)$-list-decodable.
